architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept exactly one formulation-level prediction only if Delta_bar lies in exactly one of these inclusive bands: H-LEVEL-DILUTE, -46.16% to -39.36%; H-LEVEL-ASSOC, +13.84% to +20.64%; or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC, -76.16% to -69.36%. The accepted classification must be flagged as provisional if Delta_120 and Delta_130 do not individually fall in that same band.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The directly measured S1C41 viscosity levels at 120 and 130 C remain inside the candidate-specific 80-130 C measurement support. No, this primary observable does not depend on a rheological regularity measured in the same chemistry family as S1C41: M-SWEEP measures the resin-modified chemistry directly and does not transfer the unmodified-family thermal-response shape. The relative contrast does use the frozen unmodified E2 reference, so any hypothesis classification is formulation-level and provisional because no contemporaneous matched E2 control is included.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Using Delta_bar: Delta_bar <= -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-ASSOC; Delta_bar >= -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-PLASTIC; and Delta_bar < -46.16% or Delta_bar > -39.36% falsifies H-LEVEL-DILUTE. If Delta_120 and Delta_130 imply different classifications, none of the three hypotheses is accepted and the single-summary classification is falsified as temperature-inconsistent.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run at least three independent preparations of S1C41 and at least three contemporaneous unmodified E2 preparations under matched, fully recorded histories, measure direct 80-130 C sweeps, and adjudicate the 120 C and 130 C contrasts separately before combining them. Add acrylic-only and minor-tackifier-only matched controls if independent modifier-axis attribution remains the objective.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: The predeclared processing-window contrast Delta_bar = (Delta_120 + Delta_130)/2, where Delta_T = 100 * [eta_S1C41(T)/eta_E2,frozen(T) - 1] and eta_S1C41 at 120 and 130 C is read directly from the 80-130 C sweep; Delta_120 and Delta_130 must also be reported separately.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41::M-SWEEP avoids the binding audit's prohibited shared-shape shortcut and directly characterizes the modified chemistry at 120 and 130 C. Its frozen predictions are widely separated and it uses the smallest total modifier burden among the five VOI-tied leaders. The result can classify formulation-level behavior prospectively, but cannot establish a molecular mechanism, independent modifier attribution, candidate repeatability, or thermal-hold drift.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator on card selection because S1C41::M-SWEEP is admissible, directly measures the decision temperatures, is the minimum-burden member of the stable tied top set, and no supplied single card better answers the level question. I followed the Skeptic on interpretation: the experiment is a discriminating probe rather than a definitive formulation validation, the 3.40% threshold is not demonstrated comparison precision, the historical E2 reference is not a matched control, and H-LEVEL-ASSOC versus H-LEVEL-PLASTIC remains causally entangled by the dual-axis formulation.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: Both modifier loadings are within the supplied broad evidence regions, but the external sources are analogues and the runtime prior queries returned no rows. One dual-axis composition cannot isolate AC1920, TK100, or their interaction.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for temperature because viscosity is measured directly from 80 to 130 C, including both decision temperatures. Chemistry-shape extrapolation is avoided; transferability to future one-point anchors remains unverified.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The nominal 3.40-percentage-point band comes from a sweep-fit residual, not from a replicated between-formulation contrast; it may understate practical comparison uncertainty.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: High: this card permits one preparation and does not control the historical E2 spread of 2.80-3.57-fold, including 3.57-fold at 120 C and 3.34-fold at 130 C.

action_requests.name: assess_shared_shape_applicability
action_requests.reason: The intended experiment changes chemistry relative to the family in which the shared thermal-response shape was measured; this audit determines whether one-point calibration is defensible or whether direct M-SWEEP verification is required.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The shared local thermal-response regularity was measured in the original E1–E3 reactive-core chemistry family over 80–130 °C; E1 +P is a separately verified phosphoric-acid perturbation rather than part of the primary same-composition fit. An experiment containing an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like modifier would leave that measured chemistry family. Therefore the shared-shape one-point shortcut is not admissible without a candidate-specific applicability audit; otherwise a direct 80–130 °C sweep is required.
planner.failure_mode: Uncontrolled realization of the viscosity level at the 120–130 °C application window, creating a risk that a nominal formulation will fall outside the processing-viscosity window.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: For E2, three nominal runs differed by factors of 2.80–3.57 across 80–130 °C, with sample CV values of 0.46–0.58; at 120 °C the max/min ratio was 3.57 and the CV was 0.585. This establishes that formulation identity alone does not currently determine a sufficiently controlled realized viscosity level.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Temperature response is covered by multiple six-point 80–130 °C sweeps, and realized level has repeated E2 observations despite their large spread. In contrast, isothermal behavior is represented only by single four-point 120 °C trajectories for E1 and E5 over 15–90 min, with no independent repeats. The observed 15–60 min changes differ substantially, 9.51% for E1 versus 51.54% for E5, but the sparse formulation coverage and absence of repeats leave the time trajectory least resolved.
measurement_requirements: Compare a modified candidate with the unmodified E2 reactive-core reference under matched, fully recorded preparation and measurement histories.

Measure viscosity directly at 120 and 130 °C; because the intended modifier chemistry is outside the locally measured family, use an 80–130 °C sweep unless a chemistry-support audit explicitly validates the shared-shape shortcut for the exact candidate.
Use at least three independent preparations for level determination so that candidate effects can be separated from the observed 2.80–3.57-fold E2 realization spread.

Evaluate the measured level against the frozen inert-dilution, acrylic-association, and plasticization predictions, using the applicable measurement-resolution threshold and without inferring molecular association from rheology alone.
Measure the 120 °C isothermal trajectory at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min with at least two independent repeats, keeping initial level and hold drift as separate observables.
Preserve the source viscosity units as unknown unless established by audited source evidence, and do not extrapolate beyond the measured temperature or time windows.
planner.scientific_question: At matched and controlled preparation state, does addition of an acrylic-like modifier, independently from any minor tackifier-like loading, place the directly measured 120–130 °C viscosity level above, within, or below the inert-dilution prediction by more than experimental resolution? Those outcomes would discriminate acrylic-associative elevation, inert-diluent tracking, and plasticizing-continuum depression.

planner_action_requests_after_forcing.name: assess_shared_shape_applicability
planner_action_requests_after_forcing.reason: The intended experiment changes chemistry relative to the family in which the shared thermal-response shape was measured; this audit determines whether one-point calibration is defensible or whether direct M-SWEEP verification is required.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is an AC1920/TK100-modified chemistry outside the family in which the shared thermal-response shape was established. M-SWEEP remains admissible under the binding audit because it directly measures the processing-window viscosity and verifies the candidate-specific thermal-response shape rather than transferring the unmodified-family shape. The corresponding M-ANCHOR card is inadmissible and was removed.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: A level change within 3.40 percentage points of exactly one prediction supports that formulation-level hypothesis at this composition: -42.76% supports H-LEVEL-DILUTE, +17.24% supports H-LEVEL-ASSOC, and -72.76% supports H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. This establishes level behavior, not a molecular association mechanism.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: A result at or below -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-ASSOC; a result at or above -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-PLASTIC; and a departure exceeding 3.40 percentage points from -42.76% falsifies H-LEVEL-DILUTE. Thus the conservative dilution hypothesis is rejected if the measured change lies outside its resolution band.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: If the result is not within 3.40 percentage points of exactly one registered prediction, none should be accepted. Such an outcome would indicate that the frozen level models are incomplete or that realization-state variation obscures the composition effect; the substantial historical E2 between-preparation spread would then motivate explicit repeatability and process-state control. This sweep does not determine thermal-hold drift.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity-level change at 120 and 130 C relative to the unmodified reactive core, obtained within the direct 80-130 C sweep; the sweep also yields the fitted apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: VOI-tied and fully discriminating, but uses 17.5 wt% acrylic and therefore a larger chemistry perturbation than S1C41 without adding hypothesis separation.
VOI-tied and its 20 wt% acrylic loading has directly commensurate external support, but its 25 wt% total modifier burden is larger than the minimum sufficient tied intervention.
VOI-tied and evidence-region compliant, but the 27.5 wt% total modifier burden increases departure from the characterized chemistry without increasing discrimination.
VOI-tied and pairwise discriminating, but it is the largest tied perturbation at 30 wt% total modifier and lies at the upper acrylic boundary.
It also separates all three pairs, but its 7.5 wt% tackifier loading lies above the repeatedly supported 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster, giving nonzero extrapolation risk and a lower VOI score.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41::M-SWEEP has the top VOI score of 0.6875 and separates all three registered hypothesis pairs because its predicted changes are widely separated relative to the 3.40% resolution. Its key 120-130 C observable is measured directly rather than reconstructed through an unverified shared-shape model. Both modifier axes are inside externally supported regions, and the selected tied candidate imposes the smallest total modifier burden. The main limitation is moderate realization-state risk: one sweep cannot resolve the historical between-preparation variability or thermal-hold drift, and the dual-axis composition cannot by itself establish a unique molecular cause.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five tied sweeps have identical VOI components, directly measure the decision quantity, separate all three registered hypothesis pairs, and remain inside the broad supported acrylic and minor-tackifier regions. S1C41 is chosen as the minimum sufficient intervention: 15 wt% acrylic lies in the conservative initial test band and 5 wt% tackifier lies in the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster, while its 20 wt% total modifier burden is the smallest among the tied cards. This minimizes departure from the characterized reactive-core chemistry without sacrificing discrimination.

residual_decision_risk: A single S1C41 preparation does not quantify candidate-specific realization variability.
No contemporaneous matched-history E2 control is included, so the relative level-change quantity is not directly established.
The 3.40% shared-shape regression residual is not validated as the resolution of a replicated between-formulation comparison in the AC1920/TK100 chemistry.
No predefined rule reconciles potentially different 120 C and 130 C percentage changes.
The dual-axis formulation leaves AC1920, TK100, reduced reactive-core fraction, and interaction effects confounded, so independent modifier-axis attribution is unavailable.
M-SWEEP does not determine thermal-hold drift.
The chemistry audit supports direct M-SWEEP measurements but not transfer of the unmodified-family shape; subsequent M-ANCHOR use would require verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
The stable tied top set and small margin over the first strictly lower card describe only the transparent score under the tested reweightings and do not establish scientific correctness.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection does not identify a different single supplied experiment card that answers the processing-window level question better. S1C41::M-SWEEP remains the appropriate admissible direct measurement and the minimum-burden member of the tied top set. However, its one-preparation protocol and lack of a contemporaneous matched E2 comparator mean that the resulting candidate levels cannot defensibly be treated as a relative level change resolved to 3.40 percentage points, given the historical 2.80-3.57-fold E2 between-preparation spread. The sweep may directly establish S1C41 viscosity at 120 and 130 C and its candidate-specific thermal response, but it cannot by itself support the proposed acceptance or falsification thresholds. The dual-axis design also cannot independently attribute an effect to AC1920 versus TK100 or their interaction. Replicated matched S1C41 and E2 preparations and a predefined rule for the 120 C and 130 C contrasts would be required for those stronger interpretations.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposed S1C41::M-SWEEP is in the five-card tied top set. The tied top set was unchanged in all 29 tested scenarios: top_experiment_set_stability was 1.0, every recommendation_flip_boundary was null, and every term survived scaling from 0.5 to 1.5. The base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower was 0.002292. Thus no tested perturbation, including scientifically plausible reweighting of hypothesis discrimination, uncertainty reduction, decision relevance, interpretability, budget efficiency, extrapolation risk, or process-state risk, changed the decision. Weightings outside the tested range were not evaluated and cannot be adjudicated from the payload.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary 120 C and 130 C levels stay inside measured support because M-SWEEP measures the AC1920/TK100 candidate directly across 80-130 C; it does not transfer the unmodified-family shape to reconstruct those levels. The corresponding M-ANCHOR route was correctly excluded by the binding audit. Candidate-specific replication is still required to establish practical level-change resolution, and subsequent anchor use would require this direct sweep to verify shape transferability for the same chemistry family.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: A single sweep can numerically fall on either side of the listed boundaries, but the protocol cannot generate the specified matched relative change with demonstrated 3.40% resolution because it lacks a contemporaneous E2 comparator, independent preparations, and an analysis rule for reconciling 120 C and 130 C results. Thus the stated thresholds are not attainable as defensible experimental falsification criteria under the specified protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The claim that one S1C41 sweep separates all three registered level hypotheses would confuse nominal prediction spacing with experimentally demonstrated discrimination.
objections.objection: The nominal predictions for S1C41 are separated by 30.00 percentage points (H-LEVEL-DILUTE versus H-LEVEL-PLASTIC), 60.00 points (H-LEVEL-DILUTE versus H-LEVEL-ASSOC), and 90.00 points (H-LEVEL-PLASTIC versus H-LEVEL-ASSOC), all larger than the declared 3.40% M-SWEEP threshold. However, that 3.40% is a shared-shape regression residual, not the resolution of a between-formulation level-change comparison. The protocol permits one preparation, while E2 showed CV values of 58.5% at 120 C and 54.1% at 130 C and max/min ratios of 3.57 and 3.34. Therefore the experiment does not establish that its realized comparison uncertainty is below even the smallest 30-point hypothesis separation.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result could be classified against the three frozen numerical predictions at this one dual-axis composition, but it could not support independent modifier-axis attribution or show that acrylic-like loading caused any elevation.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: 15.0 wt% AC1920 and 5.0 wt% TK100 replace 20.0 wt% of the E2 reactive core. H-LEVEL-ASSOC assigns elevation specifically to the acrylic-like axis, whereas H-LEVEL-PLASTIC assigns depression to total loading from both axes. With no acrylic-only, TK100-only, or interaction controls, the measured level cannot identify an AC1920 contribution independently of a TK100 contribution, an AC1920-by-TK100 interaction, or the reduced reactive-core fraction. The proposer admits only that a unique molecular cause cannot be established, but lists no unseparated hypotheses despite the stated scientific question requiring the acrylic effect independently from minor tackifier loading.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The percentage change used to accept or falsify hypotheses would require an unspecified historical reference, imputation, or post hoc aggregation rather than being read directly from the specified measurement.
objections.objection: M-SWEEP directly measures S1C41 viscosity at 120 and 130 C, so those absolute levels are direct observables. The proposed primary observable is instead a viscosity-level change relative to the unmodified reactive core. The stated protocol measures only one freshly prepared candidate sample and does not specify a contemporaneous, matched-history E2 control or a rule for selecting among the historically divergent E2 realizations. It also gives no rule for combining potentially different 120 C and 130 C percentage changes into the singular acceptance quantity. E_eta additionally requires the stated ln(eta) versus 1/T regression, although it is secondary to the level claim.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct level measurements remain admissible, but the proposal could overstate their quantitative discrimination precision by importing a residual scale that has not been verified for the modified chemistry and comparison design.
objections.objection: The primary 120 C and 130 C viscosity levels do not reuse the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI thermal-response shape: S1C41::M-SWEEP measures them directly and simultaneously supplies a candidate-specific 80-130 C sweep. This aspect survives the chemistry-domain attack, and the binding audit correctly removed S1C41::M-ANCHOR. Nevertheless, the 3.40% discrimination threshold comes from shared-shape/intercept-fit residual behavior rather than replicated level-change measurements in the AC1920/TK100 family, so that threshold itself is not validated as the practical resolution for S1C41.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A preparation-state fluctuation or arbitrary reference choice could be reported as falsification of a formulation-level hypothesis.
objections.objection: The inequalities are mathematically reachable, but the specified protocol cannot produce the required defensible measured level change. It has min_repeats = 1, does not measure a matched E2 comparator, and does not control the historical 2.80-3.57-fold preparation spread. The criterion that H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified by a departure greater than 3.40 percentage points therefore cannot be applied as an experimental falsification threshold with this protocol. The same problem affects comparisons to the -42.76% boundary used to falsify H-LEVEL-ASSOC and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No immediate scientific claim is invalidated on the supplied record, although the prospective status of the later grid and software should not be overstated.
objections.objection: No target wet-lab result, outcome-derived label, or post-result adjudication is visibly used in the proposed interpretation. The payload discloses that the exact v2 grid and fine-refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment and that no repository freeze artifact is available, but it also explicitly limits the historical claim to the earlier Agent recommendation and states that validation coordinates and outcomes were excluded. The proposal also correctly limits its claim to formulation-level rheology and says that neither a molecular association mechanism nor thermal-hold drift can be established by this sweep.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run the direct 80-130 C sweep on at least three independent S1C41 preparations and at least three contemporaneous unmodified E2 preparations under matched, fully recorded histories; predefine separate or combined 120 C and 130 C comparison statistics and derive the decision uncertainty from those replicated contrasts. If the scientific question retains the phrase 'independently from minor tackifier-like loading,' add matched acrylic-only and minor-tackifier-only M-SWEEP controls from the supplied candidate lattice rather than treating the dual-axis S1C41 result as axis-isolating.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The primary hypothesis-testing quantity is a change relative to unmodified E2, but S1C41::M-SWEEP specifies only one modified-sample preparation and no contemporaneous matched E2 control, despite E2 showing 2.80-3.57-fold between-preparation spread. Consequently, the protocol cannot support the claimed 3.40-percentage-point discrimination or falsification decisions.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This mandatory upstream audit must be loaded before any candidate or experiment ranking; it establishes the chemistry provenance, state-shift evidence, shared-shape support, calibration error, and hold contrast.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

tool_trace.reason: The candidate-space construction, E2 reference anchor, independent modifier axes, and historical claim boundary are needed before defining matched hypothesis-separating comparisons.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

measurement_plan.name: 80-130 C temperature sweep
measurement_plan.primary_observable: directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T
measurement_plan.protocol: Measure viscosity from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample and regress ln(eta) against 1/T.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: The measured 120-130 C level change against the unmodified reactive core falls within 3.40% of exactly one registered prediction: -47.12% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 12.88% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC or -80.87% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. That hypothesis is accepted for this composition and the processing-window level is reported with it.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The 80-130 C sweep is the direct verification measurement that establishes the thermal-response shape for a chemistry-shifted candidate.
